Go to slide 1 out of 4 Go to slide 2 out of 4 Go to slide 3 out of 4 Go to slide 4 out of 4 Overview Heart transplants are the third most common (corneas and kidneys are the most common) transplant operations in the U.S. (over 1,500 cases per year). A healthy heart is obtained from a donor who has suffered brain death but remains on life-support. The healthy heart is transported in a special solution that preserves the organ. While the patient is deep asleep and pain-free (general anesthesia), an incision is made through the breast bone (sternum). The patient's blood is re-routed through tubes to a heart-lung bypass machine to keep the blood oxygen-rich and circulating. The patient's diseased heart is removed and the donor heart is stitched in place. Review Date 4/16/2023 Updated by: Mary C. Mancini, MD, PhD, Cardiothoracic Surgeon, Shreveport, LA.
